topic_summary: Analysis of the Renaissance humanist reconstruction of Classical Latin from medieval vernacular forms. The core question is whether 'correct Latin' represents a contested kernel with two incompatible readings (medieval drift vs. classical recovery) or a D1 discontinuity where the reconstructed form was unreachable from the drifted vernacular and required reoccupation from textual symbols.

key_entities: Textual corpus (Cicero, Virgil, Livy as stabilized reference)
Living practitioners (medieval clergy, notaries, university scholars)
key_tensions: Living drift vs. textual fixity (medieval users vs. humanist philologists)
Continuity claim vs. discontinuity claim (evolutionary path vs. symbolic reoccupation)
key_mechanisms: Orthographic standardization (humanist spelling reforms eliminating medieval innovations)
Lexical archaeology (recovery of classical vocabulary from texts, rejection of medieval coinages)
key_absences: Phonological reconstruction (humanists had no access to classical pronunciation)
Sociolinguistic context of medieval Latin as functional lingua franca vs. classical Latin as elite literary register

axes.human_readable: Continuity Reading (Medieval Latin as Evolved Classical)
axes.structural_delta: Medieval Latin is Classical Latin after 1000 years of natural linguistic drift; reconstruction is correction within one evolving system
axes.primary_observable: Morphological and syntactic features traceable through continuous textual transmission; medieval innovations as extensions not replacements
axes.selection_reason: First reading of contested kernel; individually holdable position

axes.human_readable: Discontinuity Reading (Classical Latin as Reoccupied Symbol)
axes.structural_delta: Medieval Latin and Classical Latin are structurally distinct languages; humanist reconstruction required symbolic reoccupation from texts, not evolutionary reversal
axes.primary_observable: Syntactic structures in medieval Latin that are ungrammatical in classical norms; lexical items with no classical precedent; Romance substrate interference
axes.selection_reason: Second reading of contested kernel; individually holdable position

axes.human_readable: Hybrid Reading (Partial Continuity with Symbolic Overlay)
axes.structural_delta: Core morphology continuous, but syntactic and lexical layers required textual reoccupation; reconstruction was neither pure evolution nor pure symbol
axes.primary_observable: Differential success rates in reconstruction: morphology (high continuity) vs. syntax (medium) vs. lexicon (low, required textual recovery)
axes.selection_reason: Third reading of contested kernel; individually holdable position bridging the poles

axes.structural_delta: Classical pronunciation was structurally unrecoverable from texts alone; humanist Latin retained medieval phonology despite orthographic reconstruction
axes.primary_observable: Divergent national pronunciation traditions (Italian vs. French vs. German humanist Latin); absence of phonetic notation in classical texts
axes.selection_reason: Independent axis; survives pairwise test (different observable from kernel readings); addresses extraction absence

axes.human_readable: Sociolinguistic Register Shift (Functional Lingua Franca to Elite Literary Code)
axes.structural_delta: Medieval Latin was a working administrative and scholarly language; humanist Latin became a prestige literary register with restricted functional domain
axes.primary_observable: Decline in Latin notarial documents post-1500; rise of vernacular administration; Latin restricted to scholarship and diplomacy
axes.selection_reason: Independent axis; survives pairwise test (different observable and beneficiary structure); addresses extraction absence

omegas.description: Were the classical texts themselves stable? Manuscript transmission introduced variants; humanists reconstructed from already-drifted copies. The 'classical' target may itself be a moving reference.
Did any humanists attempt phonological reconstruction from meter or orthographic clues? If so, phonological_inaccessibility may be overstated as a mountain.
Did the register shift cause or follow humanist reconstruction? Causal arrow unclear; may be bidirectional feedback.
omegas.source: §3 Independence Testing (sociolinguistic_register_shift correlation with kernel readings)

fracture_scan.notes: F03 detected: phonological_inaccessibility classified as mountain but humanist attempts at phonological reconstruction from metrical evidence may exist. Generated omega_pronunciation_reconstruction_attempts to bound this uncertainty.

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The stabilized shared commitment is 'correct Latin' as a normative linguistic standard, claimed by both medieval users and humanist reconstructors as the legitimate continuation of classical authority.
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Medieval users grounded authority in continuous institutional transmission (Church, universities, notarial practice). Humanist reconstructors grounded authority in textual fidelity to classical authors (Cicero as gold standard).

readings.commitment: Medieval Latin is Classical Latin after natural linguistic evolution; reconstruction is internal correction
readings.authority_grounding: Continuous institutional transmission; living practice as legitimating
readings.expected_structural_delta: Medieval innovations treated as legitimate developments; humanist reforms as prescriptive purism

readings.commitment: Classical Latin and Medieval Latin are distinct systems; reconstruction required symbolic reoccupation from texts
readings.authority_grounding: Textual fidelity to classical authors; written corpus as sole legitimate reference
readings.expected_structural_delta: Medieval forms treated as corruptions; reconstruction as recovery of lost structure from symbols

readings.commitment: Core morphology continuous, but syntax and lexicon required textual recovery; reconstruction was layered
readings.authority_grounding: Differential weighting of transmission modes (morphology via practice, syntax/lexicon via texts)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Some medieval forms legitimate (morphology), others corruptions (syntax/lexicon); reconstruction as partial reoccupation

axiom_contradictions.basis: Continuity reading holds that living practice legitimates linguistic change; discontinuity reading holds that only textual fidelity legitimates. No single framework can hold both: either drift is legitimate evolution or it is corruption requiring symbolic recovery.
